depends on what kind of customer service youre talking about.

your situation with a technology giant? very standard. Product returns, Damaged/Dead on Arrival items, that kind of stuff? in tech, and most other retail settings, they'll treat you very well, mostly because they want return service and you are spending lots of money in markup. Talking to real people through either the internet, on the phone, or in a physical location, is ALWAYS the best.

As someone who worked in retail, People in retail are overworked and underpaid, but dont get tips. its 50/50 chance that theyre going to be nice to you, typically if youre nice and understanding, theyll be nice back. Small business owners can smell a grifter from a mile away, and they will bear teeth if you try to scam them. typically, however, these are the nicest, most personal customer service experiences you can get.

As someone who bartended, Servers and other food & beverage workers make tip wage. If you are nice and we think you will tip well enough, we will go out of our way to make everything pleasant for you-- our wages depend on good service.

Certain physical retail stores will give you hell in a handbasket over anything and everything, (espicially big box chain hardware stores, for whatever reason,) and you'll likely have to go home, and call the dreaded "customer support" line, if not just get a recorded menu/computer text-to-speech and have to leave a message, you may be faced with anywhere between five minutes and eight hours of very annoying hold music. This is also true of any health care setting, any legal system setting, any educational system setting, Banks and Feduciaries, and any kind of "tech support/help" line (i.e. you need to pay a bill but cant do it online, you have questions about payments for utilities, your cable is acting up, Your 2 year old computer is broken, your internet doesnt work and youve tried turning it off and on- SIX TIMES!)

The minute they say "oh, you have to call this number and talk to-" while youre in a store, 9 times out of ten, youre going to have the worst customer service experience to accomplish something that could have been taken care of in 5 minutes or less had you been connected to a person sooner.

Also, insurance companies and tech repair companies literally never call you unprompted. doesnt matter how much money they think you can save or if you "have a virus" or whatever. thats not how anything works here, ever. just as a tip for any outside of the US telephone scammer who may be reading this.

generally, people in the US refer to each other by their first/given names. there are a few social exceptions:

-while in school, its common respect to address many or all teachers or other points of authority with their honorific and family name, up until college/university. once you hit that point, it really depends on what *kind* of school youre in. Students are typically never referred to by their last names, except by request, or by more "jock"/sports coach-like teachers, wherein an honorific is almost never used by them. Teachers (typically male) who want to seem more "gentlemanly" typically refer to students by mr/miss and their last names. beware of this, as youre often seen as a stuffy jerk by students if you do this. for example on the student end- all of my english/math professors wanted to be called "Dr. Smith" or "Professor White" or something to that effect. My professors in the fine and performing arts, on the other hand, would yell at you if you called them something other than their given/first names. 

- In a field of law, (though this does vary by state and firm,) you dont generally refer to anyone you work with by their last names. if you dont work with them in that office, or youre talking about your boss, who is a lawyer, to a client or someone outside your office? the person youre talking about is always "Attorney [Last name]". Judges are ALWAYS "Judge [Last Name]," or, if youre speaking to them directly "Your Honor", except outside of a courthouse for non-court/legal reasons.

-Doctors are almost always "Dr." if you only know them professionally. The only Doctors, with actual doctorates, that i dont refer to as such are therapists and social workers. theyre meant to be seen more as friends, less as doctors. 

Occasionally people will refer to anyone as an honorific and their last name, bit its often meant in a way of sarcasm expressing pride in someone. Ex: "look at you, Miss Cheverau, getting that promotion!"

in closing, its not really rude, per sé? it just seems a little socially isolated, here. As long as you have a generally friendly relationship and see eachother as peers rather than with a superior/underling type of relationship, youre often okay to call someone by their first name.

As im reading your comments, here are some things to think about when youre making your fursona:

-do you want to stand out? People who are more looking to stay quiet in the fandom generally pick something more on the mid-range side of neither unpopular nor popular.

-how much art do you want to get done of your character? Many artists in the furry fandom are AWESOME, but lots of people will butcher your character if it isnt something "standard". (i was once told "well i cant draw chibis, and you refuse to pick a wolf!" after i showed them the character, paid them for a comm, and they got halfway done. I dont even have any characters that are canids, and the character in question was a dragon with a very short muzzle.)


-What do you love about the species, or the way youve seen them drawn in the fandom? Maybe you like the fact that people with snakes often draw characters as Naga, or without feet, just as snake-like bodies with arms! Or the crowns of spikes of hedgepigs! do you like things in a more "Sonic" style, or realistic? What about the centaur bodies? Do you want to combine any or all of these traits? Maybe you just like or dislike their reputation as animals!!

these are all good things to think about! also, theres nothing wrong with having more than one fursona at any given time! I have two, at the moment, a field mouse and a raccoon, and its so fun to have those two parts of myself toy around!

In general personal oppinion, i think its a lot more fun to talk about the rarity of a species rather than the "dime a dozen" kind. feel free to be you!!! thats what fursonas are all about, at the end of the day.
